summary: Sets the look of the Opportunity Map screen, including its layout, colours, cards, charts, popups and small-screen changes.
purpose: Holds all the visual rules for the Opportunity Map tool, from the main layout to fixes for phones and short screens.
why: Likely reason: keeping the look in a stylesheet lets the layout change without touching the logic. Otherwise the reason is not stated in the code.
how: The browser reads the file from top to bottom. Base rules set the layout and shared parts first. Blocks that start with a screen-size rule then change the layout for narrower or shorter screens. When two rules target the same element, the later one wins.
inputs: The class names set on the tool's elements in index.tsx, and shared colour settings such as ink, paper and red that come from the wider app.
outputs: How the Opportunity Map looks in a browser: layout, colours, sizes, which panels are shown or hidden, and where popups appear.
risks: Some rules repeat or override each other, so a change in one place can be undone by a later rule. A few rules are not scoped to this tool, so they can affect other tools.
debug: If a layout looks wrong, open the browser developer tools, select the element, and find the winning rule and its line number. Compare the screen width against the breakpoints at 1023, 900, 760 and 720 pixels. If styles seem to do nothing, check that the page is inside an element with the cpi-opportunity class. Lines 458 to 499 were not reviewed.
